sections.html:
Greenwood County lies in the western Piedmont of South Carolina, with the city of Greenwood as seat and largest community. Hodges, Ninety Six, Troy and Ware Shoals are the other incorporated places. The 2020 Census counted 69,351 residents, nearly the same as 69,661 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is 70,379.

Growth here has been slow and steady, so many houses stay with one family for decades and pass to heirs. An heir who does not plan to keep the property often finds a cash sale simpler than a listing. Lake Greenwood adds a layer of second homes, which are taxed differently from a primary residence (more on that below).

Three offices in the Greenwood County Courthouse, 528 Monument Street, deal with property tax. Each is open 7:45 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and closed on Friday.

OfficeRoomPhoneWhat it handles
Assessor109(864) 942-8537Valuation and appeals
AuditorSuite 107(864) 942-8543Homestead and legal residence credit
Tax Collector101(864) 942-3142Payments, redemptions

One rule trips people up. An appeal must challenge value, use classification or ratio. Complaining that the bill is too big is not a valid appeal, so take that to the Assessor with a specific reason.

Real estate tax here can be spread out. Advance installments are due in February, April, June, August and October, with the balance owed by January 15 of the following year.

  • Options for paying: the counter, the mail, the lobby drop box, or the county's online vendor.
  • Cash, certified checks, money orders and the major credit cards are accepted, and card payments may include a convenience fee.
  • A check drawn on an out-of-state bank will be refused for delinquent real estate tax.

Penalties follow S.C. Code 12-45-180: 3 percent once January 15 passes, 7 percent more on February 2, and 5 percent more on March 17. The Tax Collector can tell you the exact total on your own bill.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the school-tax credit
sections.html:
Three groups can apply for the homestead exemption: owners 65 or older, owners who are totally and permanently disabled, and owners who are legally blind. They need fee simple title or a life estate in their primary home, plus a full calendar year of South Carolina residency as of December 31 of the preceding tax year.

Legal residents also receive a 4 percent homeowners credit against school operating taxes, leaving only the school bond portion to pay. That credit stops short of second homes, land and business property. A lake cottage you do not live in full time is billed on a different basis than your main house, and the Assessor can confirm how your parcel is classified.

Report any sale, rental or deed change to the Auditor. At a sale the seller's exemption simply ends, and the buyer files a separate application.

Object in writing within 90 days of the mailing date when the notice raised value by $1,000 or more, as S.C. Code 12-60-2510 provides. The letter goes to the Assessor in Room 109.

Keep the letter to the point: name the parcel, say what value or classification you think is right, and give your reasons, whether that is a recent comparable sale or a condition problem the appraisal missed.

sections.h2: Farm land, rollback taxes and new construction
sections.html:
Agricultural-use classification calls for at least 5 acres in timber or 10 acres in crops, and pasture counts as crops. When the use changes, up to five years of taxes can come due. That is a real issue for anyone dividing a family tract before a sale, so ask the Assessor before you sign a contract.

Builders can seek an exemption on newly built single-family homes, and subdivision lots may qualify for a multiple lot discount. Both go through the Assessor.

sections.h2: Recording a deed and redeeming after a tax sale
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is in Room 114 of the courthouse, phone (864) 942-8612, open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. Documents delivered before 4 p.m. are recorded that day, later ones wait until the next day, and originals come back by mail 3 to 5 business days afterward.

The recording tax is $1.85 per $500 under Title 12, Chapter 24. State tax liens no longer get filed with county offices. They show up on the Department of Revenue's registry instead.

Redemptions after a tax sale go through Room 101 and are accepted as cash, certified check or money order only. Cards are not taken. Selling before the sale lets you skip that step altogether.

sections.h2: Selling a Greenwood County house with tax or title issues
sections.html:
Most sellers work through the same short list.

  1. Ask the Tax Collector what is still owed, remembering that advance installments already paid count toward the year.
  2. Find out from the Auditor whether the account carries a homestead exemption or school-tax credit, and report the pending sale.
  3. If the land is classified as agricultural and you are splitting it, ask the Assessor what rollback tax might result.
  4. Get the recorded deed from the Register of Deeds and make sure the name on it is the seller's. Inherited property needs estate paperwork in order before closing.

The three tax offices and the Register of Deeds share one building, so one trip can cover every stop, as long as you avoid Friday for the tax offices. A cash buyer purchasing as-is has no lender appraisal to wait for, so you pick the closing date around your own plans.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the tax year
sections.html:
Selling in the first weeks of the year deserves care. Between January 15 and March 17 the penalties step up, and a payoff quoted early in that stretch will be higher by the time you close. Ask for a new figure once the closing date is set.

If you already paid advance installments in February, April or June, your title agent should credit them against the balance. Bring those receipts to the closing table.

For a house nobody lives in, the main risk is an unopened bill. A bill that goes unnoticed does not stop penalties, and a tax sale can follow. An heir who sorts out the account early has more choices, including selling before the Tax Collector's office handles redemptions.

Whichever way the sale goes, keep your copies of the deed, the final tax receipt and any letter from the Auditor about the homestead exemption. Buyers and title companies often ask for them.

faqs.q: When must the last Greenwood County property tax payment be made?
faqs.a: By January 15 of the year following the tax year. Advance installments are possible in February, April, June, August and October.

faqs.q: Can I pay Greenwood County taxes over the internet?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's payment vendor handles current and delinquent real, personal and mobile home taxes, and you can also pay at the counter, by mail or in the lobby drop box. Cards may carry a fee.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for homestead in Greenwood County?
faqs.a: Owners 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind, who also meet the ownership and residency tests. File in person with the Auditor and report a sale or rental.

faqs.q: How long is the window to object to my Greenwood County value?
faqs.a: Ninety days after the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more. Send the written objection to the Assessor's office.

faqs.q: What hours do the Greenwood County offices keep?
faqs.a: The Assessor, Auditor and Tax Collector run 7:45 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and are closed Friday. The Register of Deeds is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.
